programme.title: The Magic of Making Paper that Lasts a Thousand Years: Making Hanji

programme.title: The Legacy of Joseon Ceramics: Porcelain Master
programme.desc: The Baeksan family is a traditional prestigious family that has continued Korean ceramics for over 300 years since the era of King Yeongjo of Joseon Dynasty, greatly supported by the efforts of son Kim Kyung-sik, and grandson Kim Ji-Hoon. (Provided by Korea Heritage Service, Korea Heritage Agency, K-Heritage Channel)

programme.title: The Secret Garden: Nakseonjae in Changdeokgung Palace EP.4
programme.desc: Nakseonjae combines noble residence style with palace architecture, featuring unique decorative patterns that showcase late Joseon craftsmanship. Enjoy a break at the exclusive Rear Garden of Nakseonjae in Changdeokgung Palace. (Provided by Korea Heritage Service, Korea Heritage Agency, and K-Heritage Channel)

programme.title: Mystical Hidden Scenery: Jusanji Pond, Cheongsong EP.5
programme.desc: Completed in 1720, Jusanji Pond is fed by clear waters from Byeolbawi Rock and surrounded by lush forests of Juwangsan Mountain, creating a serene, otherworldly atmosphere. (Provided by Korea Heritage Service, Korea Heritage Agency, and K-Heritage Channel)

programme.title: Coloring with Lacquer: Color Lacquer Painting Master
programme.desc: Natural pigments layered over lacquer create vivid colors that endure for generations. Each stroke, dried and painted again with care, reveals the quiet precision and artistry of Korea’s traditional lacquer painting. (Provided by Korea Heritage Service, Korea Heritage Agency, K-Heritage Channel)

programme.title: Thousands of Scissor Cuts: Preparing the Pyebaek Table
programme.desc: On the traditional wedding table, squid is transformed into a phoenix through thousands of cuts and rolls. Each motion reflects a heartfelt wish for blessings. Listen closely to the artistry of ritual cuisine. (Provided by Korea Heritage Service, Korea Heritage Agency, K-Heritage Channel)

programme.title: A Hat Full of Jeju: Cocculus Hat
programme.desc: Woven from Jeju’s native vines, the cocculus hat reflects the islanders’ harmony with nature. Once used to shield from sun and rain, it carries the quiet wisdom of a life rooted in the land. (Provided by Korea Heritage Service, Korea Heritage Agency, K-Heritage Channel)

programme.title: Striking the Jing: Brassware Master
programme.desc: With thousands of hammer strikes, the jing emerges—not just as an instrument, but as a deep, resonant voice of tradition. Made from molten copper and tin, it is shaped and tuned through breath and rhythm passed down for generations. (Provided by Korea Heritage Service, Korea Heritage Agency, K-Heritage Channel)

programme.title: Patience in Preserving Tradition: Onggi Master
programme.desc: Onggi, which every Korean household used to have at least four or five, if not dozens, were essential in traditional Korean kitchens. Feel the patience in preserving the tradition of Onggi masters. (Provided by Korea Heritage Service, Korea Heritage Agency, K-Heritage Channel)

programme.title: A Master’s Touch: Beating and Stitching Fabric
